title: v2s-bench task definition
description: One benchmark task. Lives at tasks/<tier>/<id>/task.yaml. The checker lives beside it in check/ and is never visible to skill generation.

schema_version.description: Validated for compatibility in code rather than pinned here, so a v2 record can still be read by a v1 reader that knows how.

goal.description: The task prompt shown to the agent, identical across all arms. Must state the objective without leaking the procedure.

knowledge_gap.description: The specific thing the video teaches that is required for success. The reason this task can show an effect at all.

probe_question.description: Asked of the model cold, no tools, to measure headroom (see docs/preregistration.md section 5).

probe_answer_pattern.description: Python regex, case-insensitive, that a correct probe answer must match.

taught_at.description: Timestamps in the source video, in seconds, where the gap is taught.

discoverability.description: Whether a competent agent could find the procedure from on-box documentation. Reported as a stratum: it is the main determinant of whether a skill is worth having.

image.description: Container image reference. Resolved to a digest at run time and recorded.

setup.description: Commands run before the agent starts. Must be deterministic.

network.description: Egress policy, identical for every arm. `none` is only usable when the agent runs outside the task container or needs no API (the stub). `api-only` is the normal case: the agent needs to reach its model endpoint, while the task itself must not be solvable by fetching from the open internet -- enforced by an allowlisting proxy, and the effective policy is recorded per trial. `bridge` is unrestricted egress and is recorded as a limitation, not a policy.

display.description: Provision Xvfb and a window manager (tier t3-gui).

seedable.description: Environment accepts a seed for deterministic initial state (tier t4-game).

gui_only.description: True when the task must be solved through the GUI. Roughly 15% of tasks in published GUI suites are silently solvable from a terminal, so a skill that says 'just run this command' can manufacture a large meaningless lift. The harness records action modality either way.

budget.description: Identical for every arm on a given task. An arm that wins on budget is not compared fairly.

entrypoint.description: Executable in check/, run after the agent stops. Prints one assertion-result JSON object to stdout.

required_assertions.description: Assertion ids that must all pass for the trial to count as success.

key_actions.description: Python regexes over the executed-command log. Measures procedure fidelity independently of task success.

forbidden_actions.description: Regexes whose match is recorded as a policy violation (hypothesis H7).

score.description: Optional graded outcome alongside the binary endpoint (tier t4-game).

leakage_forbidden.description: Literal strings that must NOT appear in any skill supplied to any arm: checker filenames, magic constants, oracle commands. Without this a skill becomes a hidden answer key. Enforced by `v2sbench validate --blind`.

tier.description: hermetic = rendered deterministically from a recipe; real = CC/public-domain URL. Never averaged together.

ref.description: Recipe id under videos/recipes/ (hermetic) or manifest key under videos/manifest.yaml (real).

sha256.description: Required for real videos. A mismatch invalidates the row; the harness refuses to score it.

saturated.description: Set by the calibration run. Excluded from the primary endpoint, reported in an appendix.

license.description: Required when any part of the task is adapted from a third-party suite.

oracle.description: A known-good solution that MUST pass the checker before any agent trial is run. Independent measurements put the broken-task rate in borrowed agent benchmarks at 10-15%; an oracle gate is the cheapest defence, and it also proves the task is achievable (admission criterion 3).

entrypoint.description: Executable in oracle/, run in a fresh environment. Must drive the real tool, not write the expected end state directly.

modality.description: How the oracle solves it. A GUI task whose oracle is pure shell is not a GUI task.

feedback_bandwidth.description: Whether a wrong attempt yields a diagnostic error (high) or silently produces a plausible-looking wrong result (low). A published null attributes its result to environments that already correct the agent: where feedback is high, trial-and-error substitutes for instruction. Reported as a stratum and expected to be the main moderator.

placebo_source.description: Recipe id or manifest key of the DIFFERENT video used to build this task's placebo material (arm A5). Same tool family, wrong procedure.
